identified_problem: Waskita Karya is a leading state-owned construction and engineering company that builds toll roads, bridges, dams and buildings across Indonesia; its projects are exposed to Jakarta floods and peatland fires during both construction and operation.
climate_exposure: Nationwide project portfolio includes flood-prone lowlands and fire-prone peatlands in Sumatra and Kalimantan, where design and construction decisions must account for hazard risk.
potential_pain: Designing and building in hazard zones without documented site evidence increases liability, insurance costs, and schedule/contract risk for public works.
evidence: Official site describes Waskita Karya as one of Indonesia’s largest state-owned construction companies with a 65-year track record of national infrastructure delivery.
relevant_capability: Site hazard screening and solutions intelligence (engineering options with limitations).
recommended_message: Embed Talaix flood and wildfire site evidence into Waskita’s design-build process so project teams can justify resilient siting and adaptation features.
fit_score: Large domestic engineering/construction firm executing national infrastructure in hazard-exposed regions; natural buyer of site-level hazard evidence for design and risk review.

interactions.summary: Identified via official-source research; signal: homepage presents Waskita Karya as one of Indonesia’s largest state-owned construction/engineering companies.
